enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance). Compared to last month, El Niño strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0°C, extending farther westward across the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean [Fig. 1] . The Niño indices increased, reaching +2.5°C in Niño-3.4, +3.6°C in Niño-3, and +4.4°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained significantly above average [Fig. 3] , associated with a deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Convection and rainfall remained enhanced from the central to the eastern Pacific, while suppressed conditions persisted over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were consistently negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected the ongoing evolution of El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen before beginning to weaken in early 2027 [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1038 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 852 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

 - Above normal temperatures for Saturday followed by a cold 
   front.

 - Gusty winds up to 30 mph for Saturday.

 - High chance of precipitation for middle of next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 852 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

An upper level shortwave ridge is currently parked west of 
Southern New Mexico and West Texas. This has brought us clear and 
calm conditions throughout the day. However, a positively tilted 
upper level trough will to dig further south. This will produce a 
jet streak over western Colorado and combined with a lee surface 
low will subsequently increase winds over the area. Saturday is 
forecast to be breezy and gust up to 30mph in the highlands. 
However, model and ensemble guidance are in agreement with the low
staying to our north; therefore, no wind advisories are 
anticipated at this time. Temperatures will also be above normal, 
with highs in the low 70s for the lowlands. 

As the trough attempts to push into our area, a high pressure will
push the low eastward and out of area by Sunday early morning.
This will lead to calm winds and dry conditions.While an upper
level high is parked over Far West Texas and Southern New Mexico,
a backdoor cold front will push through our area Sunday morning into
Monday which should lower our temperatures back toward near 
seasonal while keeping winds speeds fairly light around 5 to 10 
mph out of the Southeast. 

Once the ridge moves through our area, a closed Pacific Low will
trek across the desert southwest and into our area by Thursday
morning. Model and NBM guidance are fairly confident that we
should see precipitation. However, confidence is lower on the
exact precipitation type that will reach the surface, especially
in the highlands. Currently, the Sacramento mountains are forecast
to receive a wintry mix while the Gila and Black mountain ranges 
could see snow and accumulations up to 6 inches. It will depend 
on how cold the highlands get to determine how much snow, if any, 
the Gila, Black, and Sacramento mountain ranges receive. 


&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 852 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

VFR conditions are expected throughout the next 24 hours for Far
West Texas and Southern New Mexico. The main hazards are breezy
conditions on Saturday with gusts up to 30 mph around 18 to 21Z on
Saturday and winds out of the NW to NNW and scattered cloud 
coverage due to an upper level trough that will be moving into the
area. Winds should subside by Saturday night. No precipitation is
forecast for the next 24 hours. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 236 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

Somewhat elevated fire weather concerns Saturday due to dry 
conditions and breezy winds. Temperatures are expected to warm well 
above average for this time of year. In addition, 20 foot winds will 
become breezy tomorrow afternoon with speeds generally 15-25 mph 
with gusts to 35 mph possible out of the west to northwest. Dry 
conditions persist with min RHs at some locations dipping into 
critical thresholds (as low as 11%, but generally 14-20% across the 
lowlands and 30-40% in the area mountains. 

A backdoor cold front pushes in from the Great Plains Sunday morning 
shifting winds easterly with much cooler temperatures through the 
day and some light breezes. A slight increase in min RHs Sunday at 
25-35% in the lowlands and 40-55% in the area mountains. Monday and 
Wednesday will be feature breezy winds both afternoons. Min RHs dip 
yet again on Monday which may increase the fire weather concerns 
slightly. RH values will be as low as 13%, but generally 15-25% in 
the lowlands and 30-40% in the mountains. Min RHs similar on Tuesday 
with some southwest breezes that afternoon. Dry conditions persist 
until Wednesday where our next weather maker arrives. Lowland rain 
and mountain snow is possible. 

&&
